stances.instruction: Prefer the smallest local controllable-object hypothesis consistent with the reset image. Infer action meaning independently and avoid adding unobserved global mechanics.
Use an object-centric kinematic hypothesis with positions and velocities. Treat the visible objects as persistent entities and infer how the two actions perturb their motion.
Focus on the dotted diagonal structure as evidence of projectile or trajectory dynamics. Propose a deterministic action-conditioned continuation without assuming hidden observations.
Infer a plausible goal and controls from spatial layout, then implement the simplest dynamics under which the two actions could support that goal. Do not encode a preferred action.
Emphasize uncertainty in which visible entity is controlled and in the polarity of the two actions. Choose one coherent mapping that is meaningfully different from a default lateral-control reading.
Model the scene as a small discrete mode machine rather than continuous physics. Infer action-triggered phases or toggles while keeping rendering deterministic and local.
Seek a geometric transformation interpretation of the two actions, such as rotation, reflection, or structured translation of a subset of the scene. Preserve object shapes and color identities.

Construct a conservative but nontrivial countermodel that challenges the most obvious control interpretation. It must remain plausible from P0 alone and make deterministic action-conditioned predictions.
